Meta Test Description: The testcase performs PCIe device enumeration across two PCIe controller instances (DM0 and DM1). It begins by writing 0x0 to 0xE6004100 to initialize the test. It then invokes link training for the configured mode (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, or DM1_EP) using x4 lane width. Cache programming is performed by reading mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF and mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF, modifying specific bit fields (bits [14:11], [6:3], [30:27], [22:19]) using set_data() with value 0xF, and writing back. After a wait_on(20), the same coherency control registers are programmed again with all four bit groups set to 0xF in a single read-modify-write pass. The test then polls read_sii0_reg(0xC0) until (data & 0xD1) == 0xD1 to confirm PCIE0 link status, and similarly polls read_sii1_reg(0xC0) for PCIE1. Under DM0_RC mode, the Vendor ID is read from read_pcie_slv0_reg(0x0), command register is written via write_pcie_slv0_reg(0x4, 0x7), and memory base programming is invoked for both DM0 and DM1. Six SoC-level registers (0xE690000C, 0xE6900010, 0xE6900014, 0xE6900018, 0xE6900030, 0xE6900034) are written with 0x1. Cache disable programming follows by reading and modifying the coherency control registers with bits [22:19] and [30:27] set to 0x0 instead of 0xF. After wait_on(30), PCIe slave BAR registers at offsets 0x10-0x24 are written with 0xFFFFFFFF, read back, then programmed with specific base addresses (0x0, 0x4, 0x20000000, 0x40000000, 0x60000000, 0x80000000) and read back again for both pcie_slv0 and pcie_slv1. Finally, the test polls 0xE6004100 until the value equals 0x12345678, then calls finish(0).

Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Initialize the test by writing to the SoC control register. 2. Perform PCIe link training for the configured controller mode and x4 lane width. 3. Program the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register on both PCIe instances to enable cache coherency by setting specific bit fields to enable values. 4. Wait for the configuration to take effect. 5. Re-program the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register on both instances with all coherency bit groups enabled. 6. Poll the SII link status register for PCIe instance 0 until link-up is confirmed (expected status pattern observed). 7. Poll the SII link status register for PCIe instance 1 until link-up is confirmed. 8. Read the Vendor ID from the PCIe endpoint configuration space and verify it is valid. 9. Enable the PCIe command register on the endpoint. 10. Program memory base addresses for both PCIe controller instances. 11. Write enable values to SoC-level PCIe control registers. 12. Disable cache coherency by modifying the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register on both instances, clearing the relevant bit fields. 13. Wait for the disable to take effect, then confirm by re-programming with cleared values. 14. Enumerate PCIe BARs on both slave interfaces by writing all-ones, reading back to determine BAR sizes, then programming specific base addresses and reading back to confirm. 15. Poll the completion status register until the expected completion pattern is observed. 16. Report test completion.

Meta Test Description: The testcase performs PCIe DMA write and read transactions across four DMA channels on either PCIe controller instance (DM0 or DM1). It begins by writing 0x0 to 0xE6004100 to initialize the test. Link training is invoked for the configured mode (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, or DM1_EP) using x4 lane width. For DM0_RC, the test polls read_sii0_reg(0xC0) until (data & 0xD1) == 0xD1 to confirm link-up, reads the Vendor ID via read_pcie_slv0_reg(0x0), writes 0x7 to write_pcie_slv0_reg(0x4) to enable the command register, calls bar_program_dm0_x4() and mem_base_program_dm0_x4(). For DM1_RC, the equivalent operations are performed using sii1, pcie_slv1, and dm1 functions. The test then calls non_secure_prot_nic() and polls 0xE6004100 until the value equals 0x12345678. Source data is preloaded by writing 0xC0DEBEED to 128 consecutive locations starting at src_addr0 (0xE6000000) and 0xF00DDEAF to 128 consecutive locations starting at src_addr0+400. GIC is configured via GIC_Set() and GIC_EnableAllIRQ(). For DM0_RC: DMA write and read interrupt masks are cleared by writing 0x0 to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF and mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF. DMA write channels 0-3 are programmed via program_dma_wch0-3() with source, destination, and length parameters, then triggered by writing the channel number (0x0-0x3) to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF. After each channel trigger, the test waits in a while(int_pend) loop with wait_on(10) for the interrupt to fire. DMA read channels 0-3 are similarly programmed via program_dma_rch0-3() and triggered by writing to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF. For DM1_RC: the same sequence is performed using mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF, mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF, mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF, mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF, and program_dma1_wch/rch functions. The Default_IRQHandler reads mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF (or PCIE1 equivalents for DM1_RC), masks with 0x0000000F, clears the interrupts by writing the status to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF (or PCIE1 equivalents), sets int_pend = 0, and calls GIC_ClearIRQ(0x20) for DM0 or GIC_ClearIRQ(0x23) for DM1. The test concludes with wait_on(10) and finish(0).
